_comment: Yashigani kuroshio-* serving container seccomp profile (Captain finding #2 / Red-Council HIGH). SCMP_ACT_ERRNO default means every syscall not in the allow-list below is blocked with EPERM — the explicit second 'names' block naming the standard post-RCE recon/escape toolkit (ptrace, process_vm_readv/writev, unshare/clone-with-new-namespaces, mount family, keyctl family, bpf, perf_event_open, kexec_load, module-load/unload, iopl/ioperm, syslog) is REDUNDANT with the default-deny but kept explicit and documented, matching Docker's own default-profile convention, so the deny set is self-documenting rather than implicit. This profile is applied to kuroshio-classifier/kuroshio-chat/kuroshio-puller containers via compose security_opt / k8s seccompProfile.localhostProfile. Podman 6 'podman compose' v2 wrapper risk (YSG-RISK-074, finding #8): this file MUST be referenced by an explicit path in the compose overlay, never relying on default injection — see docker-compose.kuroshio.podman-override.yml.

syscalls._comment: allow-list: the syscall set llama-server + its Python control-plane sibling actually need — I/O, memory management (mmap/madvise/mprotect/futex for the model-load + inference compute path), networking (loopback to the ring-fence bridge only, enforced by the network layer not this profile), and standard process bookkeeping.
explicit deny — documented as the closed post-RCE recon/escape toolkit even though the default action already blocks these (Captain finding #2 hardening requirement, enumerated not implied).
